_comment: Timing and design thresholds shared by `showtime check` (scripts/check.mjs, before the render), `showtime qa` (lib/st/qa, on the final file) and `showtime retime` (lib/st/cli_core.py). Change them here only, so check and qa agree. min_contrast: WCAG ratio every text needs (an error for text >= 1% of the frame height). tiny_text_frac: readable text below this fraction of the frame height is a tiny_text warning (UI mockups marked data-st-decor are exempt). freeze_noise_db: the picture counts as unchanged while the mean absolute difference from the start of a hold stays under this level (qa: ffmpeg freezedetect n=, check: the same mean on its 64x36 luma samples), so small typing or a 2 px playhead is still a hold in both. label_gap_em: SVG labels in one graphic (chart values and axes, map names) that touch, or sit side by side or stacked closer than this fraction of their font size, are labels_crowded in `showtime check`. launch_hold_s: the still-hold limit for launch, promo, release and trailer films (showtime.json "kind"): a settled result or a still hook may breathe a little longer than in other videos, but the round-4 benchmark judges marked every 3.6-4.9 s still stretch in launch films as frozen, so launch films warn from 3.5 s (the end card holds up to final_hold_max_s). Phone check (scripts/lib/phone.mjs; references/qa.md): phone_width_pt is the portrait phone width a video fills; phone_min_pt is the smallest readable text in points at that width, per aspect (on-screen px * phone_width_pt / frame width; tiny_text also keeps the older floor tiny_text_frac); reading is the on-screen reading speed per language (cps = characters/s, wps = words/s, the longer time applies; no wps for languages written without spaces), plus reading_lead_s to find the text and reading_min_s as the shortest hold. Sources, checked against the published guides on 2026-09-29: references/qa.md (Phone check). hearing: the hearing pass of `showtime qa` and `review-pack` (lib/st/qa/hearing.py; references/qa.md, review.md): voice_over_bed_min_db is the least a voice line may sit over the music under it (voice_masked, measured with the render's narration stem; the mix report warns under 8 dB too), quiet_stretch_s and quiet_under_lu make near silence mid-video a quiet_stretch (and list pauses in the voice), level_jump_lu is the change at a cut the ear notices (level_jump), abrupt_end_db is how close the last 0.2 s may stay to the 3 s before before the ending counts as cut off (abrupt_end); fast_wpm, slow_wpm and sfx_loud_lu only mark lines and effects in the critic's audio.txt. speaker_gap_lu / speaker_gap_fail_lu: how far the mix above 300 Hz (a phone or laptop speaker) may sit under the full mix before speaker_loudness warns / fails; measured 2026-10-07 on every posted film at 0.7-8.2 LU and on a bass-led showreel preview at 13.6 LU (st.audio.meter; the mixer's speaker-safe step aims for 8 LU). showreel: the showreel tone (lib/st/showreel.py, scripts/lib/showreel.mjs; references/tones.md, showreel): a flash word (data-st-flash, or {flash: true} on a canvas) of at most flash_max_words words and flash_max_chars characters, on screen at least flash_min_s, may leave before its reading time (check: flash_text, not short_text), as long as one other text is held its full reading time (no_hero_line); qa warns showreel_sparse under shots_per_15s_min shots per 15 s (the round-5 blind vote of 2026-10-05 went to a reel with 13-14 shots and lost the takes with 9-11), and the docs aim for up to shots_per_15s_max; showreel_long_end when the end card holds still (nothing moves) longer than end_hold_max_frac of the duration, or the last shot runs longer than end_shot_max_frac (the losing takes held their name 2.5-3.5 s of 15); showreel_repeats when two shots of 0.4 s or more that are not neighbours look alike (colour histogram distance under repeat_hist_max and coarse layout correlation over repeat_layout_min: the same technique or layout twice); an energy dip is a stretch over dip_max_s where nothing moves much before the end card (the critic's rubric counts them). look_budget_ms: the extra time per frame a WebGL look (fluted-glass, tilt-shift, liquid-metal, mesh-gradient, god-rays, marble, metaballs; runtime/effects/gl.js) may cost without a GPU, estimated from its passes and size with the costs measured on our 64-core test machine (SwiftShader, one browser, 1080p); `showtime check` warns above it (look_budget). look_live_warn / look_live_max: the most looks on screen at once (each holds a WebGL context while its clip shows; Chrome keeps about 16 per page): check warns above the first and fails above the second (look_contexts). blur: the shutter blur on chosen elements (data-st-blur, ST.blur; runtime/stage.js, scripts/lib/blurcheck.mjs; references/stage-api.md, Shutter blur): check warns blur_slow when a blurred element, at its fastest frame, moves less than min_motion of its shorter side (as it is on screen at that frame) in one frame (the smear is then a soft edge, not motion; the snaps measured on our 64-core test machine ran 0.3 for a scale punch to 3.4 for a whip, drifts and gentle entrances under 0.1) or never moves fast enough to blur, blur_text when text is blurred for longer than text_run_s in one run, on every frame it is on screen, or with a threshold under default_threshold px a frame (the runtime's default: it blurs while it moves slowly), and blur_container when the element covers container_frac of the frame or more, holds more than container_nodes elements, is a clip holding clips, or holds a canvas or video.
